Meridian is the second most populous city in Idaho, after Boise, and it sits in Ada County. Population is 142,988 as of July 1, 2025, up from 117,635 at the 2020 census. It is the state's fastest-growing city.

The city covers about 26.8 square miles of flat ground in the north central Treasure Valley, with Boise to the east and Nampa to the west. Because it is so large and so many new builds come to market, a Meridian house competes with a deep pool of listings. That is the main reason owners with repair needs or a short timeline look at options besides a standard listing.

Meridian grew out of an irrigated farm community. The Nampa-Meridian and Settlers irrigation districts still serve the area, and several canals cross the city from southeast to northwest. That farm and canal history shows up in lot lines and irrigation easements.

When you sell, find out whether your lot has pressurized irrigation or a ditch right. Buyers ask, and a clear answer saves a round of back and forth. If the answer is not in your closing papers, the title company can help you trace it.

Most of the city lies north of I-84. Street names carry a north, south, east or west prefix measured from the corner of Franklin Road and Meridian Road. Running west to east, the major roads are Black Cat, Ten Mile, Linder, Meridian, Locust Grove and Eagle. Running north to south they are Chinden (Highway 20/26), McMillan, Ustick, Cherry or Fairview, Franklin, Overland, Victory and Amity.

Old Town centers on Main Street and Pine Street, and most industrial land runs along the railroad between Pine and Franklin. Buyers often shop by the nearest major intersection, so name those cross streets when you describe your house to a cash buyer or in a listing.

Meridian has hot dry summers and cold winters with only occasional light snow. Summer temperatures often pass 100 F, so cooling matters more than winter loads. A buyer's inspector will look at the age of the air conditioner, attic insulation and ventilation, window condition and the sprinkler system.

Replacing a failed cooling unit before a sale can be costly. A cash buyer will usually fold that into the price instead of asking you to fix it first.

Meridian Building Services handles permits for structural, fire, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work. The office is at 33 E. Broadway Ave. #102, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The phone number is 208-887-2211.

Permit applications, fee payment and inspection scheduling all run through the online citizen portal. A certificate of occupancy is issued once every required inspection is done. Remodels, fences, sheds, garages, foundations, fireplaces and demolition all need permits too.

  • Look up the permit history before you list, especially for garages, sheds and remodels.
  • Close out open permits if you can, since an open permit can delay a closing.
  • Keep final inspection records with your other home papers.

Planning and Zoning decisions affect nearby development. If your house backs up to vacant land, check the City Council hearing agendas. The council meets Tuesdays, with a work session at 4:30 p.m. and public hearings at 6:00 p.m.

The West Ada School District serves almost all of Meridian and is the largest district in Idaho. A portion of the city extends into the Kuna Joint School District 3. Buyers ask which schools serve an address, so confirm the boundary with the district instead of guessing from the city name. The district shown on your tax bill is a quick check.

Ada County bills property tax for Meridian. The full-year payment or first half is due December 20. The second half is due June 20 if the first half was paid on time.

DateWhat happens in Ada County
January 1Appraisers set market value; first day to apply for the homeowner's exemption
First Monday in JuneAssessment notices mailed
June 20Second half due
Fourth Monday in JuneLast day to appeal a value
Fourth Monday in NovemberPrimary roll bills mailed (by this date)
December 20Full-year payment or first half due

If the 20th lands on a weekend or holiday, a payment postmarked on or before the 20th counts as timely the next business day. Ada County also issues subsequent and missed roll bills for improvements and later-assessed property, due June 20. If your house was recently built or remodeled, ask the title company to look for those.

The homeowner's exemption covers 50% of the value of an owner-occupied primary home and up to one acre, with a $125,000 maximum. It lasts until ownership changes, so a buyer has to apply for their own.

Idaho law does not cap changes in assessed value. Each taxing district can raise the property tax part of its budget by no more than 3% unless voters approve more, or new construction and annexation add to the base. For questions, email taxinfo@adacounty.id.gov or call 208-287-6800.

Idaho Code 55-2504 requires anyone transferring one to four unit residential property to complete a property condition disclosure form. Nonowner-occupied rentals are included. The rule covers sales, exchanges, installment contracts and options.

Idaho Code 55-2505 exempts some transfers: foreclosure transfers, estate transfers by a fiduciary, transfers to a spouse or lineal relative, and newly built homes never lived in. Those newly built sellers must still declare annexation and city service status. If you are unsure which group you fall into, ask an Idaho attorney or title officer.

A cash sale removes the lender, so your timeline depends on title work and the closing date you choose. The steps are short:

  1. You request an offer and share what you know about occupancy, liens, back taxes and needed repairs.
  2. The buyer looks at the house.
  3. You compare the offer with listing costs, repair estimates and holding costs.
  4. If you accept, a title company runs the closing and pays off any mortgage or taxes from your proceeds.

You owe nothing if you turn an offer down. In a market as large as Meridian, a listing may suit a house in good condition, so a local agent's opinion is a useful comparison.

Before you call anyone, gather your latest tax bill, any permit paperwork and a list of repairs you already know about. Having those in hand makes the offer more accurate and the closing faster.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Meridian?
faqs.a: Ada County does. The full-year or first-half payment is due December 20, and the second half is due June 20 if the first half was paid on time.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Meridian property value?
faqs.a: The last day to submit an appeal is the fourth Monday in June. Assessment notices from the Ada County Assessor go out the first Monday in June.

faqs.q: Where do I get a building permit record in Meridian?
faqs.a: Contact Meridian Building Services at 33 E. Broadway Ave. #102, phone 208-887-2211, or use the city's online citizen portal to track permits and inspections.

faqs.q: Which school district is Meridian in?
faqs.a: Most of Meridian is in the West Ada School District, the largest in Idaho. A portion of the city extends into the Kuna Joint School District 3.

faqs.q: Does the buyer inherit my homeowner's exemption?
faqs.a: No. The exemption ends when ownership changes, so the buyer applies with the county assessor if they will live in the home as their primary residence.
